name: dev.telara/jira-gitlab-sprint-delivery-audit
description: Cross-reference a Jira Agile board's active sprint against a GitLab project's merge requests: list the sprint's issues, list merge requests updated at or after a given timestamp, and deterministically match them by scanning merge request titles, descriptions, and branch names for the sprint's own issue keys. Read-only; never creates, comments on, or transitions anything in either system. The match itself is a closed string-matching operation, not a model judgment -- no reasoning is used or required.

transform.program:
# join.star -- deterministic cross-reference of a Jira board's active sprint
# against a GitLab project's merge requests. THE JOIN. This is the only
# transform in the workflow; there is no reason: step anywhere in
# workflow.yaml, and none is needed here (see README "Key extraction"
# DECISION and requirements-checklist.json's rejected "model reasoning"
# entry). TAP transform host interface: params arrive as predeclared
# globals (sprint, issues, mrs, lookback, cap); the value assigned to
# `result` is the step's output. No I/O, no imports.
#
# Key extraction has no regex builtin in this Starlark sandbox, so it is
# done by manual character-class scanning instead: a Jira issue key is 2+
# uppercase ASCII letters, a hyphen, then 1+ digits, anchored at a token
# boundary (the character immediately before the letter run, and the
# character immediately after the digit run, if either exists, must not
# itself be alphanumeric). That anchoring is what makes this safe without a
# regex engine:
#   "Fixes ENG-123."                 -> ENG-123   (space/period boundary)
#   "feature/ENG-123-fix-thing"      -> ENG-123   (digit run stops at '-',
#                                                   which is not alnum)
#   "SUPERENG-123"                   -> no match  (letter run absorbs
#                                                   SUPERENG as one token,
#                                                   which fails the '-' check
#                                                   only if SUPERENG isn't a
#                                                   real key; a real key
#                                                   glued to a longer
#                                                   uppercase prefix is
#                                                   rejected by the
#                                                   preceding-char check)
#   "ENG-123abc"                     -> no match  (trailing alnum char
#                                                   directly after the
#                                                   digit run fails the
#                                                   boundary check)
# Extracted tokens are then matched by *exact string equality* against the
# active sprint's own issue keys -- so a candidate that happens to look
# key-shaped but belongs to no sprint issue (a different project's ticket,
# a version string, etc.) is correctly treated as "no linked sprint issue",
# not a false match.

def _is_upper(c):
    return c >= "A" and c <= "Z"

def _is_digit(c):
    return c >= "0" and c <= "9"

def _is_alnum(c):
    return _is_upper(c) or (c >= "a" and c <= "z") or _is_digit(c)

def _extract_candidate_keys(text):
    if text == None:
        return []
    keys = []
    n = len(text)
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        c = text[i:i + 1]
        if _is_upper(c) and (i == 0 or not _is_alnum(text[i - 1:i])):
            j = i
            while j < n and _is_upper(text[j:j + 1]):
                j += 1
            letters = j - i
            if letters >= 2 and j < n and text[j:j + 1] == "-":
                k = j + 1
                while k < n and _is_digit(text[k:k + 1]):
                    k += 1
                digits = k - (j + 1)
                if digits >= 1 and (k >= n or not _is_alnum(text[k:k + 1])):
                    keys.append(text[i:k])
            i = i + letters if letters > 0 else i + 1
        else:
            i += 1
    return keys

def _unique(strs):
    seen = {}
    out = []
    for s in strs:
        if s not in seen:
            seen[s] = True
            out.append(s)
    return out

def _mr_candidate_keys(mr):
    found = []
    found += _extract_candidate_keys(mr.get("title"))
    found += _extract_candidate_keys(mr.get("description"))
    found += _extract_candidate_keys(mr.get("source_branch"))
    found += _extract_candidate_keys(mr.get("target_branch"))
    return _unique(found)

def _empty_result():
    return {
        "sprint": None,
        "matched": [],
        "issues_without_mr": [],
        "mrs_without_issue": [],
        "match_rate": None,
        "counts": {
            "sprint_issues": 0,
            "matched_issues": 0,
            "issues_without_mr": 0,
            "mrs_considered": 0,
            "mrs_without_issue": 0,
        },
    }

def _join(sprint_list, issue_list, mr_list, lookback, cap):
    # The empty-sprint case is decided ONLY by whether list_sprints(state=
    # active) found an active sprint -- never inferred from what
    # list_board_issues happened to return (see workflow.yaml's comment on
    # the sprint/sprint_issues steps for why those two calls are kept
    # independent).
    if len(sprint_list) == 0:
        return _empty_result()

    active_sprint = sprint_list[0]
    sprint_issues = issue_list[:cap]

    issues_by_key = {}
    for iss in sprint_issues:
        issues_by_key[iss["key"]] = iss

    # Lookback filter: client-side, against each MR's own updated_at, since
    # the catalog's list_merge_requests exposes no server-side since/
    # updated_after query param (see README SPEC-FEEDBACK). ISO 8601
    # timestamps compare correctly as plain strings when both sides use the
    # same 'Z'-suffixed UTC format, which is what the catalog's mapping
    # returns and what inputs.updated_after is documented to require.
    considered_mrs = []
    for mr in mr_list:
        updated_at = mr.get("updated_at")
        if updated_at != None and updated_at >= lookback:
            considered_mrs.append(mr)
    considered_mrs = considered_mrs[:cap]

    matched_mrs_by_key = {}
    mrs_without_issue = []
    for mr in considered_mrs:
        linked_keys = [k for k in _mr_candidate_keys(mr) if k in issues_by_key]
        if len(linked_keys) == 0:
            mrs_without_issue.append({
                "iid": mr["iid"],
                "title": mr["title"],
                "state": mr["state"],
                "source_branch": mr.get("source_branch"),
                "target_branch": mr.get("target_branch"),
                "web_url": mr.get("web_url"),
            })
        else:
            for k in linked_keys:
                if k not in matched_mrs_by_key:
                    matched_mrs_by_key[k] = []
                matched_mrs_by_key[k].append({
                    "iid": mr["iid"],
                    "title": mr["title"],
                    "state": mr["state"],
                    "web_url": mr.get("web_url"),
                })

    matched = []
    issues_without_mr = []
    for iss in sprint_issues:
        key = iss["key"]
        if key in matched_mrs_by_key:
            matched.append({
                "issue_key": key,
                "issue_title": iss["title"],
                "issue_status": iss["status"],
                "merge_requests": matched_mrs_by_key[key],
            })
        else:
            issues_without_mr.append({
                "key": key,
                "title": iss["title"],
                "status": iss["status"],
                "assignee": iss.get("assignee"),
            })

    total_issues = len(sprint_issues)
    matched_count = len(matched)
    match_rate = None
    if total_issues > 0:
        match_rate = matched_count / total_issues  # Starlark '/' is true division -> float

    return {
        "sprint": {
            "id": active_sprint["id"],
            "name": active_sprint["name"],
            "state": active_sprint.get("state"),
            "start_date": active_sprint.get("start_date"),
            "end_date": active_sprint.get("end_date"),
        },
        "matched": matched,
        "issues_without_mr": issues_without_mr,
        "mrs_without_issue": mrs_without_issue,
        "match_rate": match_rate,
        "counts": {
            "sprint_issues": total_issues,
            "matched_issues": matched_count,
            "issues_without_mr": len(issues_without_mr),
            "mrs_considered": len(considered_mrs),
            "mrs_without_issue": len(mrs_without_issue),
        },
    }

result = _join(sprint, issues, mrs, lookback, cap)

inputs.name: gitlab_project_id
inputs.description: GitLab project ID (numeric) or URL-encoded path like 'group%2Fproject'

inputs.name: jira_board_id
inputs.description: Numeric Jira Agile board ID whose active sprint is audited

inputs.name: max_results_per_side
inputs.description: Safety cap on how many sprint issues and merge requests the join processes per side

inputs.name: mr_state
inputs.description: GitLab merge request state filter: opened, closed, locked, merged, or all

inputs.name: updated_after
inputs.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only merge requests updated at/after this instant enter the join
